issues.feedback: Marking atomic writes as out-of-scope conflicts with the stated requirement that sessions survive crashes. A crash during `fs::write` can leave a truncated JSON file and lose all previously persisted sessions. Use write-to-temp + `fsync` + atomic rename (and ideally fsync parent dir) to preserve last-known-good data.

The write-point plan misses internal rollback persistence in `rollback_current_loop`. There are real paths where rollback happens and the process returns immediately (e.g., QA/review iteration limit when `--until-complete` is false), so stale on-disk sessions can survive and violate invalidation rules.

The criterion/test of running `ralph run --loops 1` twice and expecting session reuse is not valid with current semantics: records are keyed by `loop_number`, so second invocation runs loop 2 and should not reuse loop 1 sessions. Cross-invocation reuse must be tested on the same in-progress loop (interrupted/resumed flow).

The proposed prompt-change invalidation test is incomplete: editing prompt after a fully completed loop will not trigger `RestartLoop` because `handle_prompt_change` short-circuits when no loop is in progress. Test must force an in-progress loop (e.g., `--until-review`) and set `prompt_change_action=restart-loop`.

There is a naming/location mismatch: requirements mention `session_store.json` in loop artifacts, while the spec uses `session-store.json` in project root. Pick one canonical path/name and align all acceptance criteria/tests to it.
